seoTitle: GoDaddy Website Builder: How to Use It & Plan Pricing
metaDescription: See how to open GoDaddy Website Builder from your account dashboard, choose it over WordPress, and compare what the Basic, Standard, Premium, and Ecommerce tiers actually unlock.
intro: GoDaddy sells two very different ways to get a site online: the drag-and-drop Website Builder, and a fully self-managed WordPress install. Picking the wrong one before you've built anything means redoing work later. This guide follows the path from your GoDaddy account dashboard into the Website Builder product page, shows where that choice gets made, and breaks down what separates the Basic, Standard, Premium, and Ecommerce tiers so you're not guessing which plan your site needs.
costNote: GoDaddy prices Website Builder in four tiers, Basic through Ecommerce, with the top tier priced highest because it's the only one that includes a real online store. Exact monthly figures move with promotions, billing term, and region, and GoDaddy's own pricing pages block automated fetching, so this guide describes what each tier unlocks rather than quoting numbers that may already be stale by the time you read this. Check godaddy.com/pricing directly for the current figures before choosing.

steps.heading: Start from your GoDaddy account dashboard
steps.body: After logging in, GoDaddy drops you on a personal dashboard headed "Pick up where you left off," surfacing your existing domains, renewals and billing, and a shortcut to GoDaddy Airo, the platform's AI site-building assistant. If you've never built a site here before, the "More ways to grow" section points you toward GoDaddy Website Builder as one of several add-on products tied to your domain.

image.caption: The GoDaddy account dashboard, with "Pick up where you left off" shortcuts and a prompt to explore GoDaddy Website Builder.

steps.heading: Choose between the Website Builder and a WordPress site
steps.body: Under Websites and Hosting, GoDaddy presents two paths side by side: "Create with Websites + Marketing," the drag-and-drop Website Builder with designer-made templates and built-in marketing tools, and "Create a WordPress site," for people who want to customize everything down to the pixel while GoDaddy handles hosting, maintenance, and software updates. If you want to be publishing pages within the hour without touching plugins or themes, Website Builder is the faster route. WordPress trades that speed for more control.

image.caption: The Websites and Hosting section, comparing Website Builder's templates-and-marketing approach against a self-managed WordPress site.

steps.heading: Open the Website Builder product page
steps.body: Clicking through to Website Builder lands you on its dedicated landing page, with a live preview of the editor showing a sample store page and an editing panel with Color, Font, and Buttons controls. Two buttons sit under the headline: Start for Free, which needs no credit card, and See Plans and Pricing, where the tier comparison lives.

image.caption: The GoDaddy Website Builder landing page, showing the editor preview with its Color, Font, and Buttons panel alongside the Start for Free and See Plans and Pricing buttons.

steps.heading: Understand what separates the four plan tiers
steps.body: The jump between tiers is mostly about which tools unlock, not the core building experience. The same drag-and-drop editor and templates are available from Basic onward, and Basic already includes one-time appointment bookings and a limited amount of email marketing sends per month, so appointment scheduling itself is not a Premium-only feature. What Standard and Premium add on top is higher email-send limits, SEO tools, and recurring or group appointment bookings for businesses that take repeat bookings rather than one-off ones. Ecommerce is the tier that unlocks selling: a real online store with product pages, cart, and checkout, which the lower tiers don't include at all — you'd need a separate PayPal-style button just to take a one-off payment on a Basic or Premium site.

steps.heading: Match the plan to what your site actually needs to do
steps.body: For a simple informational site — a portfolio, a landing page, a local business's hours and contact info — Basic covers it without paying for tools you won't touch. Once you need higher email-send volume, SEO tools, or repeat bookings rather than one-off ones, Standard or Premium starts to earn its higher price. Only move to Ecommerce if you're actually selling products through the site itself; if you just need a link to an existing store elsewhere, a lower tier plus that link is usually enough.

steps.heading: Build, preview, and publish
steps.body: Once you've picked a plan, template selection and editing happen in the same builder shown in the product preview: swap colors and fonts from the side panel, drag sections into place, and use Preview to check how the page reads before it's public. When the design is ready, Publish makes the site live on your connected domain immediately, and you can keep editing afterward since changes save and republish without taking the site offline.

faq.question: What's the difference between the Basic and Premium plans?
faq.answer: Basic covers the core drag-and-drop builder, templates, and one-time appointment bookings. Premium adds unlimited social connections, a much higher email-send limit, and recurring or group appointment bookings on top of that same foundation.

faq.question: Do I need the Ecommerce plan to sell products?
faq.answer: Yes. Ecommerce is the only tier with a real store: product pages, cart, and checkout. The lower tiers don't include selling functionality, only a payment button for one-off donations or purchases.

faq.question: Does Basic really include appointment booking?
faq.answer: Yes, one-time bookings are available from Basic onward. What the higher tiers add is recurring and group bookings, not the feature itself.

faq.question: Is coding knowledge required to use GoDaddy Website Builder?
faq.answer: No. It's a drag-and-drop tool with a Color, Font, and Buttons side panel for styling, so no coding experience is needed to build and publish a site.

faq.question: Can I upgrade my plan later as my site grows?
faq.answer: Yes, you can upgrade from Basic to a higher tier as your site's needs expand, without starting the build over.

faq.question: Should I choose Website Builder or a WordPress site on GoDaddy?
faq.answer: Choose Website Builder to be live quickly with templates and built-in marketing tools. Choose WordPress for full control over customization if you don't mind managing more of the setup yourself.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a walkthrough recorded in 2025. In September 2026, godaddy.com's own pricing and help pages returned 403 responses to automated fetches, so the tier feature breakdown was cross-checked against an independent, recently updated pricing tracker instead of GoDaddy's own documentation. That check corrected one claim this guide previously made: appointment booking is available from the Basic tier, not gated to Standard or Premium — those tiers add recurring and group bookings, higher email-send limits, and SEO tools. Readers should confirm exact current prices on GoDaddy's own site, since this guide intentionally does not quote dollar figures that could go stale.
